verses.commentary: A lament. Amos sings a funeral dirge for a nation not yet dead. Prophetic mourning for inevitable death. He grieves what they cannot yet see.
Fallen is Virgin Israel, never to rise again. The qinah meter, the limping rhythm of Hebrew funeral songs. Deserted in her own land. Left where she fell, unburied.
A thousand will have only a hundred left. Ten percent survival. A hundred becomes ten. Decimation upon decimation. Military power reduced to remnant.
Seek me and live. The heart of the chapter. Amid doom, an offer. The same God who judges offers life. Seeking God is the only survival.

Do not seek Bethel, Gilgal, Beersheba. The famous shrines are spiritual dead ends. Gilgal will go to exile (a Hebrew pun). Bethel (house of God) becomes Beth-aven (house of nothing). Geography cannot save.
Seek the Lord and live. Repeated command. Or he will sweep through Joseph like fire. The stakes are existence itself. Bethel cannot quench what God ignites.
You turn justice into bitterness. Wormwood, the bitter plant. Righteousness cast to the ground. Courts that should protect the poor become instruments of oppression.

He made the Pleiades and Orion. A hymn interrupts. The God they ignore made the constellations. Midnight to dawn, day to night at his command. He who calls seas to flood the land. Creator power behind prophetic words.
He flashes destruction on the stronghold. Military security vaporizes. The fortified city ruined. What armies built, God unbuild in a flash.
They hate the one who reproves in court. Truth-tellers despised. Justice advocates detested. The corrupt system punishes integrity.
You levy taxes on the poor, impose tribute on their grain. Extracting from those with nothing. Stone mansions built but never occupied. Lush vineyards planted but never enjoyed. Interrupted luxury.
I know your many offenses, your great sins. God sees everything. Oppressing the innocent, taking bribes, denying justice to the poor. The catalog of crimes.
The prudent keep quiet. So corrupt is the system that wisdom means silence. The times are evil. Speaking truth is dangerous. Prophets speak anyway.
Seek good, not evil, that you may live. The positive command. Then the Lord will be with you, as you claim he is. Their claims to divine favor are hollow without justice.
Hate evil, love good; maintain justice. The way forward. Perhaps the Lord will have mercy on the remnant of Joseph. Only perhaps. Repentance offers no guarantee, only possibility.
Wailing in the streets, cries in the squares. Public mourning everywhere. Farmers called to weep. Even those unfamiliar with formal lament will need to mourn.
Wailing in the vineyards. Places of joy become places of grief. I will pass through your midst. Like the death angel in Egypt. The God who passed over now passes through.
Woe to you who long for the Day of the Lord. They want divine intervention, imagining rescue. But for them it will be darkness, not light. They expect victory; they will find judgment.
Like fleeing a lion only to meet a bear. Like resting at home and being bitten by a snake. No escape. Safety an illusion. Danger follows them indoors.
Will not the Day of the Lord be darkness? Rhetorical question expecting yes. Pitch-dark, without brightness. Total reversal of expectations. The day they wanted becomes the day they dread.
I hate, I despise your religious festivals. Strong verbs of rejection. Your assemblies are a stench. Worship without justice nauseates God. Ritual performance without ethical substance.
Burnt offerings, grain offerings, fellowship offerings. All the standard sacrifices. God rejects them all. Not because sacrifice is wrong but because hearts are wrong.
Away with the noise of your songs. The temple music is noise to God. I will not listen to your harps. Beautiful liturgy covers ugly lives. God stops his ears.
But let justice roll on like a river. The positive alternative. Righteousness like a never-failing stream. Not occasional good deeds but constant, flowing justice. The most quoted verse in Amos.
Did you bring me sacrifices forty years in the wilderness? Rhetorical question. The wilderness generation had minimal sacrifices yet knew God. Relationship preceded ritual.
You have lifted up your king's shrine, your idol's pedestal. Astral worship, star gods. Self-made religion alongside Yahweh worship. Syncretism pollutes everything.
I will send you into exile beyond Damascus. Assyria, though unnamed. The direction specified: northeast. Into the empire that will consume them.
